children: Godavari Biorefineries Ltd has secured a patent from the China National Intellectual Property Administration for its invention titled ‘Use of compounds for treating viral infections’.
A media statement said antiviral drug development includes approaches that target host-cell mechanisms involved in viral infection, alongside those that act directly on viruses.
The patent covers compounds that inhibit Vacuolar ATPase (V-ATPase), a cellular mechanism some viruses use during infection, and their use in medicaments for treating viral infections.

This grant follows a similar patent secured earlier in Japan for the same invention, marking an important additional jurisdiction in which the company has protected this antiviral compound class, it said.

Quoting Samir Somaiya, Chairman and Managing Director of Godavari Biorefineries Ltd, the statement said: “ Our focus is on exploring how these compounds can contribute to the development of solutions that address important challenges in human health. Securing patent protection in China strengthens our intellectual property in this area and supports our continued efforts to develop original molecules through science-led research. Our long-term commitment to advancing life sciences research with the potential to create meaningful impact for human health remains a priority.”
Sangeeta Srivastava, Sandip Gavade, Maithili Athavale, and Prashant Kharkhar are the four inventors named on the patent.

title: Godavari Biorefineries secures a Chinese patent for viral infection treatment compounds
